name: Receipts
description:
Paste a job posting. Receipts checks each requirement against your real CV, shows you the evidence, and writes tailored bullets and a cover letter that use only facts you already have.

**How it works**

1. Add your CV once — PDF, DOCX or pasted text. It is split into numbered lines and saved in your Anna storage.
2. Paste a job posting. Receipts pulls out every stated requirement and marks it as evidenced, related, or no evidence yet — each one citing the CV lines that back it.
3. Ask for tailored bullets or a cover letter. Every sentence is checked by a deterministic verifier before you see it; anything the verifier cannot trace back to your CV is dropped, not softened.
4. When an interview comes, open the application again. Receipts lays out what you will be pressed on and the CV line behind every sentence you sent — your own words, in the order they will be asked for.

5. Got a CV or cover letter written somewhere else — in Word, or by another AI? Paste it into Receipts and every sentence is read against your CV, with the numbers, tools and employers it cannot back up quoted straight back at you. No model runs, nothing is saved, and it works before you have a posting at all.

6. The application form's free-text questions get the same treatment. Receipts answers them from your CV with the line cited under every sentence — and when your CV cannot answer one, it hands you the question instead of writing around it. Asked why you want the job, it writes nothing at all: a CV records what you did, not what you want.

7. And when Receipts gets it wrong, you can say so. Point at the lines on your CV that cover a requirement it missed and the correction is recorded beside its verdict — never folded into it, never counted as something the app checked. Your interview brief then reminds you that nobody but you has agreed with it yet.

**And the app checks its own work.** When a posting names a technology, a requirement can only be marked evidenced if the CV line cited underneath it actually contains that technology. If the evidence is on a different line, Receipts fixes the citation. If it is nowhere, the requirement drops to "related" and the screen says why. The verdict you read is one a rule has been over, not just a model.
6. Answer a gap in your own words and it becomes a line in your CV — stored exactly as you typed it. Receipts then tells you which of the applications you already sent that sentence would change, and, when you run one of them again, which requirement it turned from "no evidence yet" into a receipt.

**Why it is different**

Most AI resume tools improve a CV by inventing experience — metrics you never hit, tools you never used. That surfaces in interviews. Receipts refuses: a number, tool, employer or job title that is not in your CV never reaches the page. You see the gaps honestly, and what to prepare for.

**Showing your receipts**

Any match can be turned into a card you can post: the summary sentence, the requirements as shapes, and nothing else. It is built from counts alone — no line from your CV, no employer, no wording from the posting can reach it. The role title is the one thing you can add, and it is off until you add it.

**Your data**

Your CV lives only in your Anna account storage. No external services. Delete everything in one step from Your data.
_comment_bundled_executas: Handles resolved by `anna-app dev` and `anna-app apps publish`: each path is scanned for executa.json, the minted tool_id replaces every `bundled:<handle>` reference in manifest.json (in memory — the file on disk is untouched), and bundle/anna-tool-ids.js is written so the UI reads the same ids.
